title: How to Permanently Remove Glance Lock Screen Wallpaper Ads on Samsung, Realme & Xiaomi
metaTitle: How to Disable Glance Lock Screen Ads on Samsung, Realme & Xiaomi (2026)
metaDescription: Tired of invasive news, clickbait, and shopping ads on your Android lock screen? Here is how to disable Glance, Wallpaper Carousel, and lock screen bloatware permanently.

excerpt: Glance turns your phone's lock screen into a relentless billboard for clickbait articles and shopping promos. Here is how to disable it permanently across all major smartphone brands.

faq.title: Why does Glance keep turning itself back on after system software updates?
faq.description: OEMs receive revenue-sharing kickbacks from lock screen content providers. Major software updates often bundle setup wizard prompts with pre-checked 'Smart Lock Screen' agreements that re-enable Glance unless you manually untick the consent checkboxes during reboot setup.

faq.title: Does disabling Glance improve smartphone battery life and reduce mobile data usage?
faq.description: Yes! Glance runs continuous background services to download high-resolution images, video teasers, and trending news feeds. Disabling it reduces background RAM consumption by 80-150MB and prevents 500MB to 1.5GB of unwanted monthly cellular data consumption.

faq.title: Can I completely uninstall the Glance app package via ADB if the toggle fails?
faq.description: Yes. On devices where OEMs hide or disable the toggle, you can remove the package permanently via USB debugging using ADB command: `adb shell pm uninstall -k --user 0 com.glance.internet` without voiding your warranty.

html:
The Intrusion of Lock Screen Monetization

When you purchase a modern smartphone in India and emerging global markets, you might assume that your upfront hardware payment grants you complete autonomy over your operating system experience. Unfortunately, Android smartphone original equipment manufacturers (OEMs)—including market leaders Samsung, Xiaomi, Realme, Oppo, and Vivo—have increasingly incorporated third-party monetization software directly into their system firmware. The most pervasive of these built-in commercial engines is Glance (and its Xiaomi equivalent, Wallpaper Carousel).

Marketed disingenuously as a 'smart dynamic wallpaper assistant', Glance is fundamentally an aggressive, real-time programmatic advertising delivery network. Every time you press your power button to glance at the time, verify an incoming text message, or double-check a calendar notification, Glance presents clickbait celebrity gossip, auto-playing short video reels, sensationalized news snippets, and sponsored affiliate e-commerce promotions. Accidental left or right horizontal swipes hijack your touchscreen, opening resource-intensive in-app browser webviews that consume mobile cellular data and CPU cycles. This forensic tutorial explains the technical ramifications of lock screen bloatware and provides the verified instructions to purge Glance completely across all major Android skins.

The Technical Cost: RAM, Battery, and Data Overhead

Lock screen advertising services inflict substantial, quantifiable penalties on your device's hardware efficiency and daily battery longevity:

  • Background Cellular Data Consumption: Glance continuously synchronizes with remote content delivery networks (CDNs) to pre-fetch 1080p and 4K wallpaper images, interactive HTML5 cards, and streaming video trailers. On standard cellular connections, this background telemetry silently burns through 450 MB to 1.8 GB of high-speed data every single month without user consent.
  • Persistent Wake Locks and Battery Drain: The Glance background daemon (typically registered in Android OS under package names such as com.glance.internet, com.samsung.android.glance.service, or com.miui.android.fashiongallery) holds persistent CPU wake locks. By interrupting the Linux kernel's deep sleep state (Doze mode), Glance causes passive overnight battery degradation of 5% to 9%.
  • Behavioral Profiling and Privacy Leakage: Lock screen content networks monitor engagement telemetry—tracking how long your screen remains illuminated on specific articles, your device fingerprint, geographic location coordinates, and category preferences to build a monetizeable behavioral dossier.
  • Accidental Touchscreen Triggering: Because Glance repurposes standard swipe gestures across the lock screen, retrieving your smartphone from a jeans pocket frequently results in accidental clicks, unwanted video playback, and pocket dialing of sponsored landing pages.

Step-by-Step Removal Guide Across Major Android Interfaces

1. How to Disable Glance on Samsung Galaxy (One UI 5, 6 & 7)

Samsung bundles Glance under an ambiguous settings category named 'Wallpaper Services'. Follow this precise path to eradicate it:

  1. Launch the Settings app on your Samsung Galaxy smartphone.
  2. Scroll down the main settings menu and tap Lock screen and AOD (on older One UI builds, simply tap Lock screen).
  3. Select Wallpaper services.
  4. You will be presented with three radio options: Glance on Samsung, Dynamic Lock screen, and None.
  5. Tap the radio button corresponding to None.
  6. Tap the small Gear icon next to Wallpaper services if available and ensure 'Swipe left for info page' is toggled strictly to OFF. This prevents the lock screen from maintaining an active swipe-card canvas.
  7. Restart your smartphone. Your lock screen will now display strictly your designated static gallery wallpaper or lock screen widgets without dynamic third-party feeds.

2. How to Disable Wallpaper Carousel on Xiaomi, Redmi & POCO (HyperOS & MIUI 14)

Xiaomi embeds Wallpaper Carousel deeply within its system display stack. Execute these steps:

  1. Open Settings and navigate to Always-on display & Lock screen.
  2. Scroll down to the Lock screen section and select Glance for Mi (or Wallpaper Carousel depending on your regional ROM build).
  3. Toggle the primary master switch labeled Turn on to the OFF position.
  4. Xiaomi will display an exit survey dialog asking you why you are turning it off. Select 'Don't show this again' and tap Turn off.
  5. The Vital Privacy Step: Scroll to the bottom of that same menu, tap Privacy policy, and select Withdraw consent. Confirm the prompt. Withdrawing consent forces Xiaomi's local analytics client to revoke its authorization token, cutting off telemetry communications with Glance servers.

3. How to Disable Lockscreen Magazine on Realme UI & OPPO ColorOS

Realme and OPPO brand this feature as 'Lock Screen Magazine' or 'Glance for Realme':

  1. Navigate to Settings > Home screen & Lock screen.
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the list and tap Glance for Realme (or Lock Screen Magazine).
  3. Turn off the master toggle for Turn on.
  4. Ensure the secondary toggles for 'Update wallpapers using mobile data' and 'Carousel wallpaper updates' are disabled as well.

4. How to Disable Lock Screen Poster on Vivo & iQOO (Funtouch OS)

  1. Open Settings > Lock screen & wallpaper.
  2. Tap Lock screen settings.
  3. Tap Lockscreen Poster.
  4. Toggle off Lockscreen Poster Wallpaper and disable 'Update wallpapers over Wi-Fi'.

Comparison Table: Lock Screen Bloatware Across Major OEMs

Samsung Galaxy Glance on Samsung Prompted during initial setup com.samsung.android.glance.service Yes (Via ADB Shell)
Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO Wallpaper Carousel / Glance for Mi Enabled by default in Indian ROMs com.miui.android.fashiongallery Yes (Via ADB Shell)
Realme / OPPO Glance for Realme / Magazine Enabled after OTA updates com.heytap.pictorial Yes (Via ADB Shell)
Vivo / iQOO Lockscreen Poster Enabled by default com.vivo.magazine Yes (Via ADB Shell)
Motorola / Nothing / Pixel Clean Stock Android Zero lock screen ads out-of-box None (Clean firmware) Not Applicable

DNS-Level Protection: Blocking Glance Telemetry Domains

If you prefer an automated network-level barrier that neutralizes Glance even if an over-the-air (OTA) operating system update reactivates the software toggle, you can block Glance's upstream advertising endpoints using Android's native Private DNS engine. By routing your encrypted DNS queries through AdGuard or NextDNS, your phone rejects all domain lookups associated with Glance ad servers.

  1. Open Settings on your Android phone and select Network & internet (or Connection & sharing).
  2. Scroll down and tap Private DNS. By default, it is set to Automatic.
  3. Select Private DNS provider hostname.
  4. Enter the following privacy-focused DNS resolver hostname:
    dns.adguard-dns.com
  5. Tap Save.

When this resolver is active, anytime Glance attempts to contact endpoints such as api.glance.in, ad.glance.net, or telemetry.glancecdn.com, the DNS request returns an instantaneous NXDOMAIN (non-existent domain) response. As a result, Glance fails to fetch sponsored content cards and renders your clean personal wallpaper instead.

The Permanent ADB Uninstallation Method (Zero Root Required)

On certain budget carrier devices or localized carrier-locked handsets, manufacturers intentionally lock or grey out the menu toggles to prevent user deactivation. In other cases, major Android security updates silently reset the user toggle back to 'On'. To eradicate Glance permanently from user space, you can uninstall the underlying APK package via the Android Debug Bridge (ADB):

  1. Enable Developer Options: Navigate to Settings > About phone. Locate the Build number entry and tap it rapidly 7 consecutive times until a toast message confirms: 'You are now a developer!'.
  2. Enable USB Debugging: Return to the main Settings menu, open System > Developer options (or Additional settings > Developer options), and toggle on USB debugging.
  3. Connect to PC: Connect your smartphone to your laptop or desktop computer using a standard USB-C data cable. On your phone screen, a permission prompt will appear: 'Allow USB debugging from this computer?'. Tick the checkbox for 'Always allow from this computer' and tap Allow.
  4. Execute ADB Shell Commands: Open a command prompt or PowerShell window on your PC (ensure you have Android Platform Tools downloaded). Run the following commands according to your phone brand:
    • For Xiaomi / POCO:
      adb shell pm uninstall -k --user 0 com.miui.android.fashiongallery
    • For Realme / OPPO:
      adb shell pm uninstall -k --user 0 com.heytap.pictorial
    • For Samsung Galaxy:
      adb shell pm uninstall -k --user 0 com.samsung.android.glance.service
    • For Vivo / iQOO:
      adb shell pm uninstall -k --user 0 com.vivo.magazine
  5. The terminal will return the message: Success. The underlying background service is now uninstalled for the primary user. Even if you reboot your device or receive standard monthly security patches, Glance cannot reactivate because its binaries no longer exist in the active user environment.

Using Shizuku for Wireless On-Device Package Freezing

If you do not have access to a desktop PC or laptop, you can freeze or uninstall the Glance system package directly on your smartphone using Shizuku paired with Canta or App Control:

  1. Install Shizuku from Google Play or GitHub.
  2. Connect your smartphone to any local Wi-Fi network (or a secondary hotspot).
  3. In Developer options, enable Wireless debugging. Tap Pair device with pairing code.
  4. Input the 6-digit wireless pairing code into the Shizuku notification prompt. Shizuku will establish a local root-equivalent elevated ADB server on your phone.
  5. Install Canta (an open-source debloating utility). Canta will request Shizuku privileges; tap Allow all the time.
  6. Search for glance or fashiongallery in Canta's app list. Select the package and tap Uninstall or Freeze. The package will be instantaneously neutralized without tethering to a computer.

Preventative Architecture & Internal Recommendations

Eradicating lock screen advertisements is only one dimension of reclaiming control over your mobile hardware. To maintain a clean, high-performance Android experience, review our detailed guide on stopping background apps from causing battery drain, learn how to safely clean hidden junk and duplicate cache files without installing questionable booster apps, and explore the best minimalist Android launchers to reduce distraction and extend battery life.
